The Hubble Space Telescope has discovered many significant things in astronomy. It has helped determine the rate of expansion of the universe, which is crucial for understanding the universe's age and future. The telescope has also discovered black holes, providing insights into their properties and behavior. Additionally, Hubble has contributed to the study of the Milky Way, helping to determine its mass and size. It has also played a role in observing supernovae, which has led to a better understanding of stellar evolution and the life cycles of stars. The telescope has also contributed to the study of distant galaxies, allowing scientists to observe the early universe and understand how galaxies have evolved over time. Hubble's observations have also led to the discovery of exoplanets and the study of their atmospheres, expanding our knowledge of planetary systems beyond our own.

The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 kilometres along the East coast of Australia from the northern tip down to the town of Bundaberg. It is composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands, covering an area of approximately 344,400 square kilometres. The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland in northeast Australia, and a large part of it is protected by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park.

Climate change is the most significant environmental threat to the Great Barrier Reef, according to a 2014 report by the Australian Government's Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority (GBRMPA). Other major threats include decreased water quality from land-based runoff, impacts from coastal development, and persistent effects from fishing activities. The reef is also threatened by storms, coral bleaching, and ocean acidification. The 2014 report also noted that while many marine life species have recovered after previous declines, the strength of the dugong population is continuing to decline.

In addition to climate change, pollution, crown-of-thorns starfish, and fishing are the primary threats to the health of the Great Barrier Reef. Other threats include shipping accidents, oil spills, and tropical cyclones. Skeletal Eroding Band, a disease of bony corals caused by the protozoan *Halofolliculina corallasia*, affects 31 coral species. According to a 2012 study by the National Academy of Sciences, since 1985, the Great Barrier Reef has lost more than half of its corals, with two-thirds of the loss occurring from 1998 due to the factors listed above.
